back: Records stored in the order in which they were added; no ordering on a field.
Records stored in order of the key field.
Each record is stored at an address calculated from its key (hashing), so it can be accessed directly.
Sequential access reads records from the start in order. Direct access goes straight to a record's address.
Processing every record in turn: serial or sequential. Quick access to single records: random with direct access.
Divide the key by the number of slots; the remainder is the slot number. For text keys, add the character codes first (folding).
Two different keys produce the same hash value and so the same address.
Use the next free slot (wrapping round), or put the record in an overflow area.

front: How is a hashed record searched for?
back: Calculate the slot; if its key does not match, continue to the next slot (or the overflow area) until the key is found or an empty slot is reached.
